body_markdown:
Sometimes the best inspiration for a story comes from our wonderful readers. This time, the feedback came from Hagerty Media reader *CitationMan*[when he said](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/i-drove-267-miles-to-not-drive-a-slate-truck/#:~:text=The%20Slate%20echoes%20the%20lines%20of%20your%20Mid%20Century%20house!) , “The Slate (truck) echoes the lines of your Mid Century house!” That sentiment delighted me, as I am proud of my humble abode. But his statement got me thinking about homes for cars, because perhaps they can complement each other.


The comment that created a story came from the photo below (left), and I have always enjoyed parking my cars in my driveway and taking them in amid their mid-century scenery. The eaves extend significantly from the walls, so it’s fun to hang out there and watch the rain slide down the sheetmetal. While I initially considered adding rain gutters to my roof, I decided I like the clean look, reduced maintenance, and sound of water dripping across the roof. (And the London-worthy droplets look perfect on the front of my long-neglected Ford Sierra, a car that I imported from the U.K. about 15 years ago.)


Hagerty Media


[Sajeev Mehta](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/sajeev-mehta/)


There’s something therapeutic about beholding your car at its abode, especially with the tranquil sounds of nature. Rain and thunder can have a calming effect on some folks, though I quickly go inside when it starts getting intense. While I can’t bring the cars inside with me, at least they give me a little automotive therapy with no effort on their part!


I know this isn’t an ordinary question for our readers, and I hope it doesn’t fall flat on its face. I reckon we all would love to have a perfect place to keep our cars, and our car stuff, because it would all look so perfect together.


Drum roll, please! So here’s the question: **What’s Your Perfect Automotive Abode?**
